extracted.intended_audience: experimental astronomers/physicists conducting pendulum and transit-clock experiments (19th-century observatory practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and reported standards for making, recording, and reducing pendulum-vibration experiments and associated clock/transit observations (Greenwich & London experiments), plus detailed observational reporting for aurora borealis sightings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of transit observations to determine transit-clock rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Use selected observations from the Greenwich Observations (stars and Sun) to obtain the rate of the transit clock; tabulate 'Observed Place', 'Apparent Place', and 'Error of Clock' and compute 'Rate in 24 hours.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select appropriate stellar transits (e.g., Castor, Procyon, Pollux, Sirius, α, β Aquilae) and solar observations; record apparent and observed times and compute the clock error and daily rate. The text shows tables of observed/apparent times and resulting errors/rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighting and selection of observations; justification of mean rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate individual observations for quality (e.g., 'an indifferent observation of the sun', 'transit instrument was very unsteady') and justify excluding or down-weighting when instrument or observation conditions were poor; then choose a mean rate accordingly (e.g., 'seem to justify the taking —0.54 as a mean rate for the whole time').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note instrument conditions (level, meridian mark adjustment) and steadiness of clock before/after period; combine these considerations with the pattern of rates to pick a defensible mean daily rate for further reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record times by both the pendulum clock and the transit clock and compute intervals
rubrics_metrics.description: For each comparison give 'Time by Clock' and 'Time by Transit Clock', compute sidereal intervals, mean intervals and then the 'Clock rate in 24 hours.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present side-by-side times and derived intervals (sidereal and mean time) so that rate in seconds per 24 hours can be calculated. Example columns: Time by Clock, Time by Transit Clock, Sidereal Interval, Mean Interval, Clock rate in 24 hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record environmental and instrument state (barometer, thermometer, clock vibration count, observer, fresh impulse)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each experiment record barometric pressure ('Barom.'), thermometer ('Therm.'), 'Clock making N Vibrations', whether a 'Fresh impulse given', and the observer name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These experimental-context parameters must accompany each run (see repeated headings: 'Barom.', 'Therm.', 'Clock making 86405.93 Vibrations', 'Observer, Mr. T. G. Taylor' / 'Captain Sabine').

rubrics_metrics.name: Record number of coincidences and times of disappearance/reappearance/coincedence
rubrics_metrics.description: For each run list 'No. of Coincid.', times of 'Disapp.' and 'Re-app.' and the 'Coincidence' times (h m s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tabulate each coincidence event (numbered 1,2,3,...), giving minute/second times for disappearance and reappearance and the calculated coincidence time. These are then used to compute mean intervals and vibrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute arc and apply arc correction
rubrics_metrics.description: For each set of coincidence data compute 'Arc and Correction' for the arc of vibration and apply this correction to the measured mean interval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables include a column 'Arc and Correction' whose values are applied to the 'Mean Interval' before reduction to standard conditions (examples: entries like 'Arc and Correction. Mean Interval. Reduct, to 62°.' ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce measurements to a standard angle/temperature (reduct. to 62° or 72°) and compute corrected vibrations
rubrics_metrics.description: After applying arc corrections, reduce the result to a standard condition (e.g., 'Reduct. to 62°.' or 'to 72°.') and produce 'Corrected Vibrations in a Mean Solar Day' at that standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit reduction steps are shown: Mean Interval -> Correct for Arc -> Reduct. to standard (62° or 72°) -> Corrected Vibrations in a Mean Solar Day. Provide final corrected vibrations and indicate the standard used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document adjustments, maintenance and their timing (e.g., planes wiped, pendulum taken down)
rubrics_metrics.description: Note any interventions on the apparatus (e.g., 'The Pendulum taken down, the planes wiped and their adjustment examined; and the Pendulum replaced.') and indicate experiments before/after such maintenance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State when adjustments were made, since these may change subsequent vibration results; separate experimental series accordingly (Exp. 1, Exp. 2 ... with notes about 'fresh impulse' or 'pendulum taken down').

rubrics_metrics.name: Report observer identity and attribute measurements
rubrics_metrics.description: List the observer for each measurement or set of coincidences (e.g., 'Observer, Captain Sabine' or 'Observer, Mr. T. G. Taylor').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include observer names alongside data rows to show who performed the timing; used throughout the tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide full tabulated raw data and intermediate reductions
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish full tables showing raw times, coincidences, arc corrections, mean intervals, reductions and final corrected vibrations; include units and labels (h m s, m s, seconds, vibrations per mean solar day).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper communicates all intermediate quantities (observed/apparent times, errors of clock, barometer, thermometer, arc corrections, mean intervals, reductions to 62°/72°, corrected vibrations). This transparency allows verification and recomputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of clock rate by comparison with transit clock and propagation of that rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain the rate of the local clock from comparisons with the transit clock while transit observations for the transit clock's rate are being made; then use those transit-clock rates to determine the rate of the coincidence clock for the experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text states: 'The rate of the clock was obtained from comparisons with the transit clock at the time that the observations were making for the determination of the rate of the latter ; thus resting the accuracy of the results on the correct determination of the rate of the transit clock.' Use selected transit observations to determine transit-clock daily rate, then apply to experimental comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: When only one star is observable, pair with solar observation to equalize weighting
rubrics_metrics.description: If only one star is available for a given time, use a solar observation occurring at the same time in conjunction with that star to more nearly equalize the share of credit among results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text recommends using two observations (star + sun) when only one star could be taken, 'thereby more nearly equalizing the share of credit to be attributed to the several results.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicitly note and use instrument instability or poor observations to explain discordant rates
rubrics_metrics.description: If rates on particular dates are in poor accordance, explicitly note causes (e.g., 'indifferent observation of the sun', 'transit instrument was very unsteady, requiring adjustment...') and use this explanation when deciding how to treat those data in overall means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use instrument inspection and sequence of clock behavior before/after the suspect period to justify down-weighting or exclusion (example: choosing -0.54 as mean because clock was steady before and since).

rubrics_metrics.name: For aurora observations: report detailed geometry relative to magnetic meridian and temporal evolution
rubrics_metrics.description: When describing aurora, report the arrangement and progress: position (compass points), elevations (degrees above horizon/zenith), breadth (degrees), streamers' directions relative to the magnetic meridian, presence of multiple arches, abrupt terminations, changes in streamer angles with movement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The aurora section gives precise reporting conventions and findings: e.g., 'streamers... placed cross-wise in relation to its own line, and all directed towards a point a little south of the zenith'; 'arch moves southward, contracting its lateral dimensions... till... a narrow belt, 3° or 4° only in breadth, stretching across the zenith at right angles to the magnetic meridian.' Report stepwise morphological changes and their directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multi-station/simultaneous observations and parallax to estimate auroral height; prefer detailed single-station particulars
rubrics_metrics.description: To infer height (e.g., Dalton's inference of 100 miles), rely on observations made at distant places at the same time and use parallax; nevertheless the Royal Society prefers minute details of separate observations from observers with favorable vantage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author contrasts general descriptions with 'details of separate observations' and presents a 'decisive' single observation that bears on height. Provide either carefully synchronized multi-station data for parallax or detailed, minute single-station evidence when arguing elevation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe successive stages and repeatability (multiple arches and progressive behavior)
rubrics_metrics.description: Record whether several successive arches appear simultaneously within the field of view and describe their successive behavior (rise, contraction, change to narrow belt, subsequent enlargement), since this affects interpretation and comparison between observers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper emphasizes that several arches often appear and that their progression (from broad low-elevation arch with crosswise streamers to narrow belt at zenith, then re-expansion after passing zenith) is characteristic and must be noted.
